title: invoice, budget & export — wireframe notes and backlog sketch
body:
Purpose / context:
This doc is a working writeup for the console experiences related to invoices, cost allocation exports, and budget/alert flows. Goal is to align simple export CSVs for accounting, provide actionable budget alerts for engineers/product managers, and design an intuitive invoice list/detail + download UX for self-serve finance teams.

High-level requirements (from PM kickoff):
- Invoice list: quick filter (by month, customer org, payment status), one-click PDF/CSV download, show rounding/credits line.
- Cost allocation export: ability to export per-route, per-model, per-team breakdown for any time window; include sampling/aggregation modes.
- Budgets & alerts: org-level and project-level budgets, weekly digest + threshold alerts (50/75/90%), optional webhook/pager duty integration.
- Auditability: include invoice id, billing period, metered units, unit prices, discounts, and committed-reserved adjustments.

Wireframe notes (desktop flow):
1) Invoices list view (left column)
   - Topbar: month picker (calendar dropdown) + org selector + search by invoice id
   - Table cols: invoice date | invoice id | amount (USD) | status | downloads (PDF / CSV) | actions (dispute / view)
   - Row hover state: quick preview (first 3 line items summary) + badge for "contains committed usage"
   - Bulk actions: multi-select -> bulk-download ZIP or mark as reconciled

2) Invoice detail (right flyout)
   - Header: invoice id, billing period, download buttons (PDF / CSV / Quick-export to SFTP)
   - Line-items: hierarchical list (model charges -> route charges -> token breakout). Each line has a small chart sparkline for trend over billing period.
   - Notes section: manual finance notes (editable for org admins) + linked payment tx ids

3) Cost allocation export builder modal
   - Step 1: choose time range (preset: last 7/30/90/365 days) or custom range
   - Step 2: group by (model / route / team / tag) - multi-select allowed
   - Step 3: aggregation level (raw line items | hourly aggregates | daily aggregates)
   - Step 4: columns checkbox list (date, org, project, model, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, inflight_cache_hits, price_per_unit, subtotal, credits_applied, net_total)
   - Options: include KV cache savings estimate (on/off), detach sample rows for large exports (>1M rows)
   - Output: CSV compatible with QuickBooks/NetSuite, and smaller "summary" CSV for BI ingestion

4) Budget creation & alert rules (console page)
   - Create budget wizard: name, scope (org/project/model/tag), amount, cadence (monthly/quarterly/annual), alert thresholds (percentages), notify channels (email, slack webhook, pagerduty), actions (auto-throttle routes / signal to routing policy to fallback cheaper models).
   - Example rule: "Auto-alert at 75% with Slack to #product-alerts, throttle non-critical experimental routes at 90%"

Acceptance criteria (minimal):
- Finance can download an invoice PDF and a CSV that mirrors the PDF line items for at least 6 months of history.
- Product/Infra users can export a per-route, per-model CSV at daily resolution for a 30-day window within < 10s for medium orgs (~500k tokens/day).
- Budget alerts reach configured endpoints and include a link to run the cost-allocation export for the last 7 days.

Backlog slices & grooming notes (suggested priorities):
- INF-2374 (P0): Invoice list + download (PDF) + audit fields (due date, taxes)
- INF-2398 (P1): Cost allocation export builder MVP – grouping by model/route, daily aggregates, CSV export
- UX-512 (P1): Budget creation wizard (UI only) + local validation of fields
- SRE-1043 (P2): Backend export job streaming & resumable export for >100k rows
- INTEGRATIONS-67 (P2): Webhook/pagerduty delivery for budget alerts (retry/backoff)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- CSV column set: do we include derived KPIs (cost per 1k tokens, median latency) or keep purely billing fields? (Finance wants derived KPIs; infra wants separate BI job)
- Data retention: exports historically should map to the same SKU/price used at the time — we need a price-history table. Who owns the data contract? (billing team)
- Auto-throttle action: should console expose immediate toggle that changes routing policy, or only suggest manual change? Legal might require human approval for changes affecting billing.

Design constraints and notes:
- For large orgs we must avoid a synchronous export that times out; plan streaming CSV to GCS/S3 and send signed URL via email/slack.
- Use same token breakdown terminology as API docs (tokens_in/out, cache_hits) to avoid naming mismatch. Add glossary tooltip on export modal.
- Accessibility: downloadable table must be keyboard navigable and labeled for screen readers.

Proposed next steps (short term):
- Design: create 3 mid-fidelity wireframes for invoice-list/invoice-detail/export builder (Sophie) — due 2024-11-20
- Engineering spike: SRE to prototype streaming export + signed URL delivery (Miguel) — 2 weeks
- Legal/Compliance check on auto-throttle action and export data retention (Priya) — block if flagged
- Sync: 30-min grooming on 2024-11-12 to convert the backlog slices to tickets and estimate story points.

Notes from prior discussion: (copied from #billing-ux slack)
- "Finance needs a CSV that groups by customer-project and can be ingested into NetSuite without transformation" (Finance: L. Chen)
- "We should include a sample schema row in the export modal so customers know column names before export" (Infra: M. Alvarez)

Quick mockup text labels (for handoff):
- Export modal primary CTA: 'Generate export' (creates job)
- Download button on invoices: 'Download PDF' and small caret -> 'Download CSV'
- Budget alert copy: 'You've used 78% of your monthly inference budget' -> CTA: 'View breakdown'

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: Export jobs overload storage / blow S3 egress budget. Mitigation: throttle job concurrency by org, require large exports to opt into storage to customer-managed bucket.
- Risk: Mismatch between PDF and CSV line items. Mitigation: canonicalize billing aggregation logic in a shared library, add unit tests, and include hash in PDF footer linking to same export job id.

Appendix: example CSV header recommendation (one-line):
"invoice_id","billing_period_start","billing_period_end","org_id","project_id","model","route","date","tokens_in","tokens_out","cache_hits","unit_price_usd","subtotal_usd","credits_usd","net_usd"

Comments welcome — add inline in this doc or ping in slack #billing-ux.
